# Proposal: Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Tamarack Instruments
**Basis:** Discovery call of 6 October 2026 with Dana Whitfield, Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg (roles of Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg: Unknown)
**Decision requested by:** 15 December 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It has about 1,100 staff, is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has not completed a prior Academy program, so this proposal starts from the Profile Block rather than from a previous baseline.

The Client's AI portfolio spans three stages. A customer service chatbot is deployed on the support portal. AI visual inspection is being piloted on the German production line. AI sales forecasting is planned for next year. The Client describes its AI maturity as Piloting.

Four facts shape this proposal. First, a June 2026 internal audit finding recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems. Second, you have set the objective of having governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027. Third, the Client intends to begin ISO/IEC 42001 work next year, with the start date not yet fixed. Fourth, the Client operates under the EU AI Act and GDPR, requires customer data to stay in the EU and consults the German works council before anything touches production staff.

The Client reports ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 as incumbent frameworks. This proposal does not assume which registers, processes, controls or records exist under them. Their scope and status are Unknown and will be confirmed at intake.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory at Piloting Maturity

At Piloting maturity, governance decisions are made at the same pace as deployment decisions. One system is live. Another is moving toward production with a fixed internal date. A third is about to enter design. A single assessment would capture the position at one point in time. It would not travel with the Client as each system changes stage.

Fractional advisory provides a steady senior presence through that transition. The work proceeds under three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. In practice this means production decisions are paced to evidence, each AI use is documented with a stated purpose before it scales and accountability stays with named Client decision makers. The advisor recommends. The Client decides.

The engagement draws on two open frameworks: the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). Executive and board briefings reference AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). Because the materials are public, the Client keeps the method after the engagement ends.

## 3. Annual Arc

The quarters below are engagement quarters. The engagement start date is Unknown. If work begins in January 2027, Quarter 2 coincides with the stated Q2 2027 production target. Whether Q2 2027 refers to a calendar or fiscal quarter is Unknown and will be confirmed at intake.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize.** The first priority is to respond to the internal audit finding. The advisor will guide the Client in building an AI system inventory covering the chatbot, the visual inspection pilot and the planned forecasting use. The quarter will also define AI governance roles and decision rights, draft an AI policy aligned with the incumbent management systems and begin a documented risk and impact assessment of visual inspection. Questions on how the EU AI Act and GDPR apply to each system will be framed for verification by counsel. The advisor will not settle them. Works council consultation timing for visual inspection will be raised for the Client to determine. Consultation status is Unknown.

**Quarter 2: Production Readiness for Visual Inspection.** The aim is to set up a documented go or no-go decision for visual inspection that the executive team owns. The advisor will help mature the operating controls for human oversight, monitoring and change management. The quarter will also assemble the decision evidence and support the executive decision. The production date is the Client's to set. The advisor's role is to make sure the decision is informed.

**Quarter 3: Deepen Toward ISO/IEC 42001.** If the ISO/IEC 42001 start date falls here, this quarter will include a readiness gap assessment against the standard. The work will draw on the inventory, policy and Quarter 2 evidence. Planned sales forecasting will go through the governance intake process before build begins. The chatbot will be reviewed for documentation and EU data residency. How the chatbot currently handles data location is Unknown.

**Quarter 4: Assure and Evolve.** Audit preparation reaches its highest intensity in this quarter. Activities will include evidence collection health checks, an internal audit readiness exercise with the Client's internal auditors and a management review rehearsal. The quarter closes with a renewal options discussion. If the ISO/IEC 42001 timeline shifts, audit preparation intensity moves with it. All outputs speak to readiness. No certification or audit outcome is promised.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

| Element | Frequency | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Executive advisory session | Monthly | Decisions, risk position and regulatory developments flagged for counsel verification |
| Governance working session | Monthly | Artifact development and implementation guidance |
| Asynchronous availability | Ongoing | Defined categories: governance interpretation, artifact review, framework application and executive decision preparation |
| Quarterly governance review | Quarterly | Progress against the arc and next quarter plan |

Attendance for each session will be confirmed with you at intake. Possible participants include the General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and internal auditors.

## 5. Scope and Out of Scope

**In scope:** governance evolution, implementation guidance, audit preparation, AI strategy and executive decision support.

**Out of scope:** legal advice, certification body functions, staff augmentation and incident command. The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions are routed to external counsel. Regulatory developments are flagged for verification and are never given as settled advice.

## 6. Investment

The engagement runs for 12 months, is renewable and is priced at US$10,000 per month. The total for one year is US$120,000. The Profile Block records an approved budget of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. How the fees split across fiscal years depends on the Client's fiscal year dates and the engagement start date, both Unknown. We ask that you confirm both so that budget alignment can be settled before signature.
